We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by going through the details again to make sure I understand everything correctly. I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200 a month, which is market rate where we live, so that's fair. I don't see any issue with that. I pay rent, which I think gives me some privileges, like being able to say no when they ask for help with things like groceries or yard work. I mean, if I were paying rent elsewhere, I wouldn't have to help my landlord with their groceries, right? But recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of that, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to just lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. So, the other day, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to help bring in the groceries, and I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was really into the game and didn't notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute. He said that "in a minute" was now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. That led to a huge shouting match, and now they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're using him as the golden child, comparing him to me, which is really frustrating. I mean, I could have gotten up and helped them, but I thought because I pay rent, I have the right to say no sometimes. Am I the asshole here? Hmm, let's break this down. First, I'm paying rent, which is fair, so I'm contributing financially. But living with parents often comes with certain expectations, even if you're paying rent. Maybe I'm not considering their feelings or the fact that they're doing me a favor by letting me live there cheaply. When they asked for help, I was dismissive, which might have hurt them. They had to remodel my section, so maybe they're stressed about that too, which added to the tension. I was playing a game when they needed help, which might have seemed like I wasn't prioritizing them. Grabbing the controller and the shouting match probably escalated things. Now they're so upset that they're checking into a hotel, which is a big deal. They might feel that I'm not respecting their space or their requests, even though I'm paying rent. On the other hand, I feel like I'm an adult and should have the right to say no sometimes. But maybe in this situation, it's more about how I responded. I could have said no politely or explained that I was busy, but instead, I was dismissive and then got into a shouting match. That probably made things worse. Also, comparing me to my brother who's doing well might be a way for them to express their disappointment or frustration with me. It's not fair to compare siblings, but they might be feeling that way because of the situation. So, am I the asshole? I think I might be, but not entirely. I was in the wrong for how I responded, especially the shouting match and dismissing their request. But I also feel like I'm an adult and should have some boundaries. However, living with parents, even if paying rent, might require some give and take. Maybe I could have handled the situation better by acknowledging their request and finding a compromise, like helping after the game or taking a break to assist them. In the end, the shouting match and the way I handled their request probably made me the asshole in this situation. I should have been more considerate of their feelings and the situation they were in, especially after the remodel. It's a tough spot, but communication and compromise are key.
